extracted.intended_audience: newspaper editors and reporters covering wartime developments (also general newspaper readers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implicit editorial standards for reporting and editing newspaper copy about unfolding wartime events (verification, attribution, cautions about censorship and unconfirmed reports). Useful to editors and reporters preparing wire copy and updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat unconfirmed reports with great reserve
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The phrase appears in context of a warning from British official quarters about reports (e.g., that Norway was preparing to negotiate). Use caution when repeating reports from uncertain or single sources; explicitly flag them as unconfirmed and avoid presenting them as established fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribute reports to sources / official quarters
rubrics_metrics.description: Versions differ but agree on several essential points; reports come from British, French and German governments and other named sources (e.g., Stockholm, DNB, BBC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always attribute claims to their originating source (government communiqués, specific news agencies, broadcasts, named officials). Make clear which side issued the report and whether other sides confirm or deny it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify broadcast reports before repeating
rubrics_metrics.description: The Stockholm wire said Emden had been sunk and CBS picked up the broadcast; the BBC subsequently denied it had broadcast the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not republish or treat as authoritative a report derived from another broadcaster until verification; note denials and corrections prominently when they occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note censorship and its effect on reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: “MILITARY CENSORSHIP HINDERS SOMEWHAT THE RAPID AND ORDERLY DESCRIPTION... THE CHIEF DIFFICULTY IS UNCERTAINTY OVER POSSIBLE GREAT SEA AND AIR BATTLES IN THE NORTH SEA.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform readers (and editors) when censorship or restricted communications limit reporting. Explain that information flow may be delayed, partial, or routed through official channels under censorship, and caution about relying on censored dispatches as complete accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use official communiqués and government statements as primary leads but with caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of official communiqués (e.g., 'A quiet on Lorraine and Alsace fronts' from the Allied command) are used as lead information in dispatches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead items on military developments can legitimately rely on official communiqués, but present them as the government's account and balance with other sources or caveats when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide optional update insertions for breaking developments
rubrics_metrics.description: “TO COVER DEVELOPMENTS THE FOLLOWING MAY BE INSERTED AFTER SECOND GRAPH...” (followed by suggested copy to update the story).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edit copy may include prewritten insert paragraphs to update breaking developments—publishers/editors may insert these after specified graphs to reflect latest claims or losses. Use them only when applicable and clearly attributed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag and explain possible duplication and uncertainty in casualty/ship-loss reports
rubrics_metrics.description: “THERE MAY BE SOME DUPLICATION IN THESE REPORTS... ALL WE KNOW OF A CERTAINTY IS THAT ALLIED AND GERMAN NAVAL AND AIR WITS...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple claims of sinkings or casualties circulate, warn readers about duplication and uncertainty; avoid aggregating unverified tallies without cross-checking and note where reports may overlap or contradict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify propaganda-controlled reporting and label accordingly
rubrics_metrics.description: German war correspondents are organized into 'propaganda companies' (articles generally appear labeled merely 'Pp. K.'), and their reports are sorted and distributed to different papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about reporting that originates from state-controlled or propaganda organizations; readers should be informed of possible editorial control or censorship influencing eyewitness dispatches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid speculation; frame analysis with qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: “THIS STATEMENT NATURALLY IS SUBJECT TO QUALIFICATIONS... IF THE NAVAL BATTLES ARE UPSET... THEN ...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opinion or analysis about the strategic effect of battles should be clearly qualified. Avoid definitive judgments when outcomes are still contingent; present plausible scenarios with explicit qualifiers and the assumptions they rest on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain delays and alternate reporting routes for isolated capitals/areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Much factual news of the German occupation has come from Berlin; Oslo and Copenhagen were isolated so news often came by courier to Stockholm or via correspondents working under local constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tell readers how and why information from particular locations is delayed or rerouted (couriers, routed through other capitals, correspondents' offices), so they understand timeliness and provenance of dispatches.
